overall: The AG found the Brockton School Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law as alleged on any of the complaint's three points, but recommended amending the February 27, 2024 executive session minutes, which lacked a substantive summary.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee improperly discussed a matter in the February 27, 2024 Purpose 2 executive session.
allegations.key_passage: After speaking with Attorney Spatafore, we are satisfied that the Committee’s discussions of the contracts fit within the parameters of executive session Purpose 2.

allegations.summary: Complaint suggested the Committee discussed potential discipline of the Superintendent in the Purpose 2 executive session, based on later conduct.
allegations.key_passage: We find no evidence that the Committee discussed the discipline or dismissal of Superintendent Thomas during the Purpose 2 executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee did not let the Superintendent speak on his own behalf before voting to place him on paid administrative leave.
allegations.key_passage: It is not a violation of the Open Meeting Law for a public body to vote on a topic without first taking comments from the public or specific individuals.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a roll call vote was required to adjourn the executive session portion of the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: A roll call vote is not required to exit executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee discussed the Superintendent in open session although the topic was not listed on the notice.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find no violation of the Open Meeting Law where the Committee discussed a topic in an open session which was noticed as an executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee improperly voted twice on placing the Superintendent on paid administrative leave.
allegations.key_passage: Nonetheless, the Open Meeting Law does not dictate the content of a discussion at a meeting and once a meeting begins, the public body controls its own agenda.

allegations.summary: Not raised in complaint; AG noted the February 27, 2024 executive session minutes lacked a substantive summary of the discussion.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law requires that meeting minutes include more than a statement that a public body held a discussion about a specified topic; the Law requires that the minutes summarize the discussion that was held.

remedy: Amend the February 27, 2024 executive session minutes to comply with G.L. c. 30A, § 22(a) (recommended, not ordered).
remedy_passage: We recommend that the Committee amend its February 27, 2024, executive session meeting minutes in accordance with the requirements of G.L. c. 30A, § 22(a).
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
